title: Enhanced Coulomb pseudopotentials in high-pressure hydrides from first principles
abstract: In the Eliashberg theory of superconductivity, Coulomb interactions oppose the phonon-mediated attraction and suppress the superconducting critical temperature $T_{\mathrm{c}}$. However, most first-principles predictions continue to treat this repulsion with an empirical Coulomb pseudopotential $μ^*_{\text{ME}}$ in the range 0.1-0.15. Here we present first-principles calculations of the Coulomb parameter $μ$ and pseudopotential $μ^*_{\text{ME}}$ in superconducting hydrides across a range of pressures. The screened Coulomb interaction is evaluated at the random phase approximation level with the Mantel code. We demonstrate that several hydride systems, including H$_3$S, YSbH$_6$ and Mg$_2$IrH$_6$, have strong Coulomb repulsions driven by a large density of states at the Fermi energy, $N_{\mathrm{F}}$. For Mg$_2$IrH$_6$ we obtain $μ=0.62$ and $μ^*_{\text{ME}}\approx0.39$, leading to a 40 K suppression in $T_{\mathrm{c}}$ relative to a standard $μ^*_{\text{ME}}=0.16$. Our obtained $μ^*_{\text{ME}}$ is far above the conventional range and, accounting for the energy dependence of the density of states, resolves the factor-of-two discrepancy between $T_{\mathrm{c}}$ estimates of previous studies. Across all systems and pressures studied, we find that $μ$ closely tracks $N_{\mathrm{F}}$, suggesting that commonly used $μ^*_{\text{ME}}$ values lead to overestimated $T_{\mathrm{c}}$ in materials where the density of states at the Fermi energy is large.
summary: This work calculates the Coulomb pseudopotential ($\mu^*$) from first principles for superconducting hydrides under high pressure. By moving beyond empirical values, the authors show that strong Coulomb repulsion significantly suppresses the superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$). This provides a crucial, more accurate theoretical framework for predicting high-temperature superconductivity in these materials.
main_problem: Accurately determining the Coulomb pseudopotential ($\mu^*$) in the Eliashberg theory of superconductivity, as standard empirical values are insufficient for high-pressure hydrides.
main_result: The authors find that strong Coulomb repulsions, quantified by $\mu^*_{	ext{ME}} \approx 0.39$ for $	ext{Mg}_2	ext{IrH}_6$, significantly suppress $T_c$ compared to standard estimates, resolving previous factor-of-two discrepancies.
method: First-principles calculations using the Random Phase Approximation (RPA) to evaluate the screened Coulomb interaction, followed by solving the Eliashberg equations in the variable density of states (vDOS) form.
model_or_system: The study focuses on superconducting hydrides ($	ext{H}_3	ext{S}$, $	ext{YSbH}_6$, $	ext{Mg}_2	ext{IrH}_6$) under high pressure, treating superconductivity via the electron-phonon coupling mechanism modified by Coulomb repulsion.
key_observables: Superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$), Coulomb parameter ($\mu$), and Coulomb pseudopotential ($\mu^*_{	ext{ME}}$).
important_parameters: High density of states at the Fermi energy ($N_F$), and the pressure range studied.
main_assumptions: The use of the Random Phase Approximation (RPA) for the screened Coulomb interaction and solving the Eliashberg equations using the vDOS form.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the inadequacy of empirical $\mu^*$ values, presents the first-principles calculation methodology using RPA for the screened Coulomb interaction, and concludes by demonstrating that the calculated $\mu^*$ leads to a substantial suppression of $T_c$ in specific hydride systems.
why_interesting: While focused on superconductivity, the rigorous, first-principles calculation of electron-electron interactions ($\mu$) and their impact on pairing mechanisms is highly relevant to understanding strongly correlated electron systems where simple models fail.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Parity plot for the ambient pressure metallic elements, comparing the µ value calculated with the PBE functional in Mantel to those obtained in Ref. [30]. The grey region indicates a fractional difference within ±10%.

FIG. 2: Comparison of impact of exchange-correlation potential on the µ value. The values are largely insensitive to the choice of functional, with discrepancies driven by changes in the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.

FIG. 3: Periodic table of the ambient pressure metallic elements, with the value of Coulomb parameter µ given with the LDA, PBE and PBEsol functionals. The colour is set by the PBE value, shown in bold. The elements Cr to Ni are excluded due to their formation of magnetic ordering, which typically precludes conventional superconductivity. The LDA for La is omitted due to the lack of a pseudo-dojo pseudopotential.

FIG. 4: Plots of the diagonal of the isoenergy averaged screened Coulomb interaction W(ε, ε). Data from Ref. [25] is shown in red and from this work in blue. The Fermi level is denoted by the dashed line. Note the different energy ranges for (b) and (d).

FIG. 5: Comparison of a range of superconducting hydride systems. Each subfigure shows the density of states, the diagonal W(ε, ε) and horizontal W(ε, 0) cross sections, and a colourplot of the full matrix. The same colour range is used across all systems, illustrating the screened Coulomb matrix elements are strong for H3S, and weak for LaSc2H24.
